scenario: AITA for offending a friend after she rejected help she asked for? | Hello! I'll try to be brief. Friend (28F) let's call her *Jade* was spoiled financially from age 12 to 18 by father and developed habits of eating out, eating premade stuff, never cooked, best brands of candy every day. At 18 dad cut her off (he and the mother are divorced), and now for past 10 years she's struggling with meeting ends working part time jobs. This year it hit really hard since her government-welfare ended. Now, she, her mom, and her brother (18M) are living from mom's 300 eur salary. Jade by being really picky with food is actually starving. She claims that she needs about 7 euros per meal that she would eat. She refuses to cook and now, they don't even have a stove to cook on, just microvawe. Me (24F) I grew up in a bit more financially responsible family and we barely eat out, we cook at home and usually bring meals to work, ect. Despite meeting ends well, I manage to make a "price" of meal about 2-3 euros. It is simple but healthy food, usually rice or buckwheat + some meat, eggs, bread, vegetables. It doesn't even get that repetetive for me even though the meals do look absolutely basic. Well, Jade, being my friend for 11 years, has been opening up and complaining lately, a lot. She actually is starving. She said lack of chocolate drives her crazy, and that she barely eats anything at all because mother doesn't give her money to eat (and she doesn't like to eat what mom buys). She asked for help. I offered dark chocolate since we have a lot at home. *Rejected.* I offered to cook to her rice, buckwheat, eggs, give her vegetables, fruit, bread. *Rejected.* I kept offering help and she said I'm offering her food that she "doesn't like" and if I want to help I should give her cash. I do want to help her, but not in cash, since she would spend it in 2 days what I could make food for 1 week with the same amount. I was offering healthy stuff that I eat myself, but it is not good enough to her. Well, I snapped and said "let me know when poverty and starvation lowers your standards". AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation with my friend Jade. Let me start by understanding the background. Jade has had a pretty privileged upbringing financially, but things changed when her dad cut her off at 18. Now, she's struggling financially, living with her mom and brother, and they're barely making ends meet. She's really picky about her food and refuses to cook, which is making things even harder for them. She's actually starving because she won't eat what her mom buys, and she's asking for money to buy her own meals. On the other hand, I grew up in a more financially responsible family, and we usually cook at home, bringing meals to work. I'm able to make simple, healthy meals that cost about 2-3 euros per meal. I offered to help Jade by giving her dark chocolate and cooking her some rice, buckwheat, eggs, vegetables, fruits, and bread. But she rejected all my offers, saying that she doesn't like the food I'm offering and that if I want to help, I should give her cash instead. I really want to help her, but I don't want to give her cash because I know she'll spend it in a day or two on things that aren't necessary, like more expensive food or treats. I offered her healthy food that I eat myself, but it's not good enough for her. Finally, I snapped and said, "Let me know when poverty and starvation lower your standards." Now I'm wondering if I did the right thing or not. First, I need to consider why I reacted the way I did. I was trying to help Jade by providing her with healthy, affordable food options. But she kept rejecting my offers, insisting on getting cash instead. This made me frustrated because I knew she wouldn't use the money wisely. I wanted to help her in a way that would actually make a difference, not just give her money that would be gone quickly. When I snapped and made that comment, I was probably feeling exasperated and maybe even a bit hurt that she didn't appreciate the help I was offering. I was trying to set boundaries by saying that I would help her only if she was willing to lower her standards, which I thought were unrealistic given her financial situation. But now I'm questioning whether that was the right approach. Did I consider her feelings and perspective? Was there a better way to communicate my frustration and set boundaries without making her feel judged or criticized? I also need to think about the dynamics of our friendship. We've been friends for 11 years, so there's a history there. I know that she's been struggling financially, and she's opening up to me about her situation. But she's also being very picky about her food, which is contributing to her problems. I want to support her, but I also don't want to enable her behavior by giving her cash that she might not use responsibly. Maybe I should have approached the situation differently. Instead of offering specific foods, I could have asked her what she would like to eat and tried to accommodate her preferences within the budget. Or perhaps I could have suggested ways for her to improve her financial situation, like finding a better-paying job or learning to cook affordable meals. I also need to consider how my comment made her feel. Did it come across as judgmental or dismissive? If so, that might have hurt her feelings and damaged our friendship. It's important to communicate in a way that shows empathy and understanding, even when setting boundaries. In the end, I want to help my friend without enabling her negative behaviors. Finding a balance between offering support and encouraging responsible decisions is key. Maybe I should have had a more open conversation with her about her financial situation and how we can work together to find solutions that work for both of us. I also need to reflect on my own feelings and why I reacted the way I did. Am I projecting my own values onto her, or am I truly trying to help her in the best way I can? Understanding my own motivations can help me approach the situation more effectively in the future. Overall, I think I need to communicate more clearly and empathetically with Jade, expressing my desire to help while also setting boundaries that respect both of our needs. It's a delicate balance, but it's important for maintaining a healthy friendship.
